title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Letter
summary: A young engineer finds an old letter in a lighthouse and learns why the lamp has never gone out.

cover.scene: Flat 2D illustration: a tall white lighthouse on a rocky coast at night, a warm beam of light across a stormy sea, a small figure at the door, no text

chapters.title: The Last Inspection
sentences: Nora was a young engineer, and her company had sent her to inspect the old lighthouse on Gull Rock.
The government planned to replace its lamp with an automatic system, so someone had to check the equipment.
She travelled by boat on a grey morning, and the waves made her feel slightly sick.
The building was cold and damp, and the iron stairs groaned under her boots.
At the top she found a heavy brass lamp that was still polished as if somebody cared for it.
That surprised her, because the last keeper had left the island almost forty years earlier.
Behind a loose panel she discovered a yellow envelope with her own surname written on it.
The handwriting was careful and slightly shaky, and the paper smelled of salt.
She hesitated for a moment, then carefully opened it and began to read.
The letter was addressed to whoever would one day come to switch the light off.

quiz.q: Why was Nora sent to the lighthouse?
options: To check the equipment before a change
To work as the new keeper
quiz.explain: The lamp was going to be replaced by an automatic system.

quiz.q: What surprised Nora about the lamp?
quiz.explain: It looked as if somebody still cared for it.

quiz.q: What did she find behind the panel?
quiz.explain: It was a yellow envelope with her own surname on it.

chapters.title: The Light That Stayed On
sentences: The writer was her great-grandfather, Elias, who had been the keeper of the lighthouse for thirty years.
He explained that a terrible storm had once destroyed a fishing fleet while the lamp was dark.
After that disaster he promised himself that the light would never fail again.
He had trained local volunteers to take turns, and the village had carried on the work after he died.
Nora realised that the polished lamp was not a mystery but the result of years of quiet devotion.
He ended the letter by asking her to decide carefully, because progress was not always a bad thing.
A machine might be more reliable, he admitted, but it could never replace the people who cared.
She went down to the village that evening and met an elderly man who confirmed the story.
His family had polished that lamp every Sunday for generations, simply out of gratitude.
Nora wrote a new report that recommended keeping the old lamp as a backup and honouring the volunteers.
Her manager was sceptical, but the village celebrated, and the light shone over Gull Rock that night as always.

quiz.q: Why did Elias promise that the light would never fail?
options: A storm destroyed boats when it was dark.
quiz.explain: A fishing fleet was lost during a storm while the lamp was dark.

quiz.q: Who kept the lamp polished after Elias died?
quiz.explain: Local volunteers carried on the work for generations.

quiz.q: What did Nora recommend in her report?
options: Keeping the old lamp as a backup
quiz.explain: She recommended keeping the old lamp as a backup.
